messages:
morgan: heads up — we're seeing a customer complaint about elevated p95/p99 latency starting ~10:04 UTC. this happened right after canary rollout v7.3.1 to eu-west. alert from perf-monitor: p99 up ~3x.

jia: on it. which canary percentage did we push?

morgan: 10% traffic to canary pool. canary config: kernel=matmul-v2, quant=4bit, batching=auto.

carlos: repro steps? any query patterns?

morgan: reproducer from support ticket included a 1k token gen with streaming. they sent spans — tail latencies spike after token 200.

lina: :eyes: attaching quick trace snippet from the user (sanitized) — looks like repeated kernel context switch / gpu queue stalls.

morgan: pasted trace: ```
> span_summary: send_request -> runtime_dispatch -> kernel_launch (matmul-v2) -> wait_sync -> kv_cache_update -> stream_write
> observed stalls at kernel_launch 3-8ms -> actually 30-50ms in p99
```

devon: did we change kernel selector heuristics in 7.3.1? I thought we only toggled quantization fallback.

jia: yes we updated kernel selector to prefer matmul-v2 for sequence_len > 512 (PR #4321). canary should pick that.

carlos: quick idea — if kernel is slower for this workload, fallback path might be slower due to additional memcpy or sync. can we check canary vs baseline kernel timings?

lina: running quick aggregation on perf-db for last 2 hours. sql: ``SELECT kernel, p95_latency_ms FROM kernel_metrics WHERE model='rwkv-13b' AND region='eu-west' AND ts > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 HOUR) GROUP BY kernel``

lina: results: matmul-v2 p95=210ms, matmul-v1 p95=78ms, matmul-v2 p99=480ms, matmul-v1 p99=120ms.

morgan: that's a smoking gun. matmul-v2 much worse for p95/p99. any changes in batch sizing?

jia: auto-batching unchanged. but matmul-v2 introduced a new warp-coarsening path that uses a different kernel for certain sequence lengths — possibly memory fragmentation.

devon: can we quickly rollback kernel selector on canary? or force canary to use matmul-v1 for seq <= 2048?

carlos: schedule: two options — 1) flip selector on canary (fast, safe), 2) rollback canary binary to 7.3.0 (slower, but safer if other regressions). Any preference?

morgan: do 1) first. flip selector, keep monitoring. if still bad, do 2).

jia: doing selector flip now: `./deployctl set-canary-config --pool canary-eu-west --kernel-selector 'prefer:matmul-v1 for seq<=2048'`

sre-bot: deploy job started (job id d8f2). 3 nodes being updated.

lina: after flip — re-aggregating: matmul-v2 p95 still high but traffic proportion to v2 dropped to 4%. overall p95 for the model dropped from 180ms->95ms in 5m window.

morgan: customer confirms lower latency in ticket. :thumbsup: but need long-term fix — matmul-v2 seems to degrade at tail.

devon: opening an incident PR to hold this — will bisect PRs that touched kernel selector / matmul path in last 2 weeks.

carlos: also check quantization path — 4bit kernels had a fallback code path that can trigger extra copies when mixed-precision changes mid-seq. could explain spikes after token 200 when precision switches.

jia: good point. run quick check: query logs for events where precision_changed=true within a single request.

lina: query: ``SELECT count(*) FROM request_events WHERE precision_changed=true AND ts > ...`` -> returns ~120 events in canary pool in last hour. baseline pool shows 3 events.

morgan: that's surprisingly high. are we enabling dynamic precision during generation?

devon: PR #4299 introduced a dynamic-quant switch to save tokens; it had a guard but might be misfiring for some seq shapes. adding to bisect list.

carlos: mitigation checklist: 
- pin kernel selector to matmul-v1 for now (done)
- disable dynamic-quant switching in canary (safe flip)
- add an autoscaling buffer to canary pool to reduce queueing while we investigate

jia: I'll disable dynamic-quant on canary: `./deployctl feature-toggle --canary canary-eu-west --feature dynamic-quant --state off`

sre-bot: feature toggle applied to 3 clusters.

lina: recomputing metrics: dynamic-quant events now ~2 in last 10m. overall p99 back to ~110ms.

support-bot: ticket #C-8221 updated: customer notified that we rolled back kernel selector on canary and are investigating root cause.

morgan: thanks. next steps for root cause:
- devon/carlos/jia to bisect PRs touching kernel selector / dynamic-quant in last 14 days (assign owners)
- add unit+perf tests to simulate the precision switch mid-sequence (devon)
- create an e2e perf job that runs synthetic long-stream workloads against matmul-v2 on our staging rigs (lina)

devon: assigned. starting git bisect across master -> last 14 days. will post commits as I find suspects. ETA 3-6h.

carlos: I'll prepare a microbenchmark (script in infra/perf/bench/matmul_tail.sh) that reproduces the 1k token streaming pattern and run it against both kernel binaries.

jia: also scheduling a controlled canary ramp test to 30% with observability hooks (traces + flamegraphs) so we can capture any regressions before full rollouts. planned in 24h once we have a patch.

morgan: good. one more ask from Support — can we add a short incident note in the internal runbook with the mitigation steps that Support can reference? (they need to respond to customers).

support-bot: internal note created at https://redwood.internal/notes/INC-2250 (private) with steps: revert selector -> disable dynamic-quant -> monitor for 30m -> escalate.

lina: devon found a likely culprit commit: `commit 9f3a2` changed the precision-guard logic, causing rare mid-seq flips when tokens contained long whitespace runs. reproducer attached in PR comments.

devon: verifying locally — running benchmark now. preliminary numbers: with 9f3a2 p99=430ms, without it p99=110ms.

morgan: if confirmed, plan: revert that commit in a patch release (7.3.2) and re-run canary with matmul-v2 and dynamic-quant ON to ensure fix.

carlos: agree. prepare rollback PR and a follow-up test. I'll also add an assertion in the kernel selection unit tests to avoid selecting matmul-v2 for sequences hitting the pattern.

devon: PR opened: #4352 revert 9f3a2 (patch). requesting quick review.

jia: LGTM, merging and triggering canary rollout.

sre-bot: patch rollout started to canary (job id a2c9). will report status.

lina: monitoring: after patch, canary p99 ~115ms, p95 ~90ms. matmul-v2 regained acceptable numbers.

morgan: closing loop with customer — replied in ticket with root cause and ETA for stable patch.

support-bot: customer replied: "thanks for the quick fix — we saw immediate improvement". ticket marked resolved pending 48h no regression.

morgan: big thanks to everyone. action items captured. I'm going to update the postmortem template once this stabilizes.

devon: saving perf logs and bisect notes in /internal/incidents/INC-2250/ for postmortem.

carlos: lesson: new kernel paths need targeted long-stream perf tests + precision-switch synthetic cases. adding to release checklist.

morgan: end of thread.
